methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort (n=79) with EWGSOP2-compliant sarcopenia assessment combining CT-derived TPAI, handgrip dynamometry, and SARC-F functional screening. Appropriate statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox multivariate regression). Main limitation: TPAI cutoff values (6.04 men, 4.98 women) derived from same cohort using ROC analysis—introduces overfitting risk. Authors acknowledge this and recommend external validation. Limited nutritional data despite known interaction with muscle mass.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort study of gastric cancer demonstrating prognostic value of sarcopenia. Clear clinical endpoints: OS 21 vs 17 months (p=0.042), multivariate HR=1.8 (95% CI 1.1-3.2, p=0.03) independent of age/BMI. Direct relevance to perioperative risk stratification and prehabilitation planning. However, limited translational data—no intervention trial or biomarker validation.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned reporting with clear methodology, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and statistical approach. TNM staging, surgical details, and Clavien-Dindo complications systematically documented. TPAI measurement protocol well-specified. However, no explicit data availability statement. Anthropometric and nutritional variables assessed but not included in analysis—gaps in reporting rationale. Follow-up data limited (median 18 months).

novelty_literature.justification: Sarcopenia and TPAI as gastric cancer prognostic factors well-established. Study contributes by integrating EWGSOP2 functional assessment with CT measures and providing longitudinal TPAI data. However, mechanistically incremental—confirms known association without new mechanistic insight or therapeutic approach. Cohort-specific cutoff values limit generalizability.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written with logical structure and clear presentation of methods and results. Tables comprehensively detail clinicopathological characteristics and survival data. Figures effectively display TPAI trajectories and Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations including small sample size, cohort-specific cutoff overfitting, and retrospective design. Minor redundancy in stating need for external validation.

key_strengths: EWGSOP2-compliant sarcopenia assessment integrating CT-derived TPAI with muscle strength and functional performance—comprehensive rather than imaging-only approach
Clear prognostic endpoints: independent multivariate association with OS (HR 1.8, p=0.03) and trend in DFS (p=0.055)
Longitudinal TPAI measurement at 6 and 12 months postoperatively—adds temporal dimension lacking in prior studies
Clinically actionable thresholds proposed (6.04 men, 4.98 women) with clear acknowledgment of overfitting risk
Well-reported STROBE-aligned methodology with transparent discussion of limitations
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=79) with limited events (30% mortality) reduces statistical power and confidence intervals for subgroup analyses
ROC-derived TPAI cutoff values specific to study cohort introduce high overfitting risk; authors correctly note external validation required before clinical implementation
Nutritional status assessed during routine care but excluded from analysis despite known major influence on muscle mass and outcomes—incomplete confounding adjustment
Retrospective design precludes causal inference; associations may reflect surgical selection (laparoscopy less frequent in sarcopenic patients)
Limited generalizability: single Spanish center, elderly population (median age 74), no prospective validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective study confirming prognostic value of EWGSOP2-defined sarcopenia in gastric cancer with practical clinical thresholds. Appropriate for tier 3 publication pending prospective validation of proposed TPAI cutoffs and inclusion of nutritional parameters.
